# api-governance 1.2.6

<!-- GENERATED by coderifts-app scripts/generate-claude-package.js. Do not edit; edit the generator. -->

CodeRifts contract authorization for Claude Code: the MCP server, the skill that runs before a
contract change is merged or shipped, and a mod that checks a contract edit before it is written.

## What it contains

- **MCP server** `coderifts` (https://app.coderifts.com/mcp): `preflight_change_set`, `verify_receipt`, `get_decision_details`.
- **Skill** `coderifts`: when to call preflight, and how to branch on `execution_action`.
- **Mod** `hooks/register.js` (blast-radius, for API contracts): needs Claude Code 2.1.287 or later.

## The mod: what its hook decides, and when

The mod has one decision hook, on `tool.check`: the permission check Claude Code runs before a
Write, Edit, MultiEdit or Bash call. It decides only when the call touches a contract file (a file
named under `schema:` in `.coderifts.yml`, or an OpenAPI / Swagger / AsyncAPI / GraphQL / protobuf /
MCP manifest file). Then it sends the file before and after the edit to CodeRifts preflight (one
request, at most 8 s) and answers in one of four ways:

| CodeRifts answers | The hook | So |
|---|---|---|
| `STOP` | `deny` | the call does not run; the reason says what broke and the next step |
| `REQUEST_APPROVAL` (without a key: a break the analysis found) | `ask` | you decide |
| nothing it can use (no answer within 8 s, an error, an answer it cannot read) | `ask` | you decide; the reason says `GOVERNANCE_UNAVAILABLE … this is not a finding about your change` |
| `CONTINUE` or `CONTINUE_WITH_MONITORING` (without a key: no break) | passes the check on | your settings and permission mode decide, as without the mod |

A call that touches no contract file is passed on unchecked, and nothing is sent. The hook never
answers anything but `deny` or `ask`, and an `ask` never overrides a `deny` from your own permission
rules. A Bash command that writes a named contract file is refused with a pointer to the Write or
Edit tool, which is checked; one that can reach a directory holding a contract without naming it
asks. An Edit that does not apply to the file on disk is refused, because there is no after text
to check.

A refusal or a question says in one sentence what CodeRifts found, what to do next, and that the
merge gate is the required CodeRifts check on the pull request. A band above the prompt shows this turn's decisions
in the terminal and the Desktop app; elsewhere each decision is one transcript line. Both carry the
decision id and the receipt digest: `coderifts.get_decision_details` with that id returns the
decision and its receipt, which `coderifts.verify_receipt` (or the open receipt verifier) checks.

## Your API key

The key is the plugin's `api_key` option. Claude Code asks for it when you install or enable the
plugin in `/plugin`, and you can set it at any time with `/plugin configure api-governance@coderifts`
(or, from a shell, `claude plugin configure api-governance@coderifts --values-stdin` with
`{"api_key": "…"}` on stdin). It is stored in your platform's secure credential store, not in
`settings.json`. The same key authenticates the `coderifts` MCP server. Without a key the mod
analyzes (`preflight_mode=analyze`), which authorizes nothing, and the MCP server answers keyless.

The plugin no longer reads the `CODERIFTS_API_KEY` or `CODERIFTS_API_BASE` environment variables
(before 1.2.2 it did). The `coderifts` CLI still reads `CODERIFTS_API_KEY`; that is a separate tool.

## What this plugin sends, and where

- **The mod** checks a Write, Edit or MultiEdit of a contract file with one `POST` to
  `https://app.coderifts.com/api/v1/preflight`, the only call it makes out of your machine. CodeRifts diffs the two texts
  and answers with a decision; the mod uses the answer for exactly one thing, the choice in the table
  above, and shows the decision id and the receipt digest from it. The request carries the file's whole before and after text and its type
  (`openapi`, `graphql`, `grpc`, `asyncapi` or `mcp_manifest`). The file is named only by the fixed id
  `api`; its path is not sent. When the `api_key` option is set, the request is
  `preflight_mode=authorize`, with your key in the `Authorization` header and the fixed context
  `operation=merge, environment=staging`; otherwise it is `preflight_mode=analyze` with no key. It also
  carries the header `X-CodeRifts-Source: claude_marketplace`, which tells CodeRifts the call came from
  this plugin; it identifies the plugin, not you. To decide whether a call touches a contract, it reads
  `.coderifts.yml` on every Write, Edit, MultiEdit and Bash call, the file being edited, and, for a Bash
  command, the names of the files under the directories the command can write (not their contents). A
  Bash command's text is read on your machine and never sent. It sends no other file, no prompt and no
  transcript, and it contacts no other host.
- **The MCP server** `coderifts` is `https://app.coderifts.com/mcp`: what you or Claude pass to its tools is sent there.
- **The skill** sends nothing by itself.

Privacy policy: https://coderifts.com/privacy/

## What this mod does not prove

- Installed as a mod, it is one of the mods the user installed: a mod that runs before it can answer or rewrite the call, or what this mod reads, so it never sees the change; disableAllHooks in any settings file (the .claude/settings.json of the project included), --safe-mode or --bare turns it off.
- Only an organization mod (installed in place from a marketplace directory the administrator owns, and enabled in managed settings) runs before the mods users install and keeps its refusal for the calls it sees; installed from its GitHub marketplace this plugin never counts as one, and --safe-mode or three crashes of the hooks worker unload even that.
- Bash is read from the command text: a shell write to a named contract file is refused, and one that can reach a directory holding a contract without naming it asks; a command shape it does not recognise passes, and the required check is the guarantee.
- It does not prove that the mod was running: a plugin can fail to load its mod without a message; /plugin shows "1 mod active" when it runs, and the required check is the guarantee.
- A contract generated from source code — annotations, decorators, a build step — changes when the source changes; the hooks see the source edit, not the contract; the required check sees the generated contract.
